topic.title: Visual Evidence Use in Vision-Language Models
topic.overview: Vision-language systems must align visual representations with language while ensuring that images contribute to the answer. This topic studies language priors, selective training, efficient multimodal computation, and fine-grained perception. The representatives ask both how to connect pretrained components and how to identify examples or tokens whose predictions genuinely depend on visual evidence.
topic.whyItMatters: A model can answer familiar questions from linguistic shortcuts while missing small but decisive image details. Training and evaluation should distinguish visual contribution from fluent guessing and account for the cost of repeated inspection.
topic.evolution: Earlier papers examine language modulation and visual-question-answering biases. Later work improves alignment with frozen language models. Recent examples quantify visual information gain, study retrieval-induced distraction, and distill region-level supervision into single-pass perception, aiming to make visual reliance stronger without expensive inference-time tool use.
openQuestions: Can visual contribution be measured without rewarding sensitivity to irrelevant pixels?
How can region-focused supervision improve detail recognition without weakening global understanding?

papers.title: Mitigating Mask Prior Drift and Positional Attention Collapse in Large Diffusion Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Two training-free decoding interventions reduce repetition and improve visual grounding in diffusion vision-language models, especially for long descriptions.

papers.title: MoDA: Modulation Adapter for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding in Instructional MLLMs
papers.tldr: MoDA uses instruction-guided channel modulation to improve fine-grained visual understanding across three multimodal model families with minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: ModernVBERT: Towards Smaller Visual Document Retrievers
papers.tldr: ModernVBERT is a 250-million-parameter visual document encoder that outperforms some retrievers up to ten times larger.

papers.title: Multi-Label Test-Time Adaptation with Bayesian Conditional Priors
papers.tldr: BCP improves frozen vision-language models' multi-label predictions by learning label co-occurrence priors from unlabeled test data.

papers.title: MVI-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Robustness to Misleading Visual Inputs in LVLMs
papers.tldr: MVI-Bench evaluates misleading visual inputs and finds substantial robustness weaknesses across 18 vision-language models.

papers.title: Neutral-Reference Prompting for Vision–Language Models
papers.tldr: NeRP corrects prior-dominated vision–language predictions, improving unseen-class recognition while preserving known-class performance in the reported benchmarks.

papers.title: OmniVL-Guard: Towards Unified Vision-Language Forgery Detection and Grounding via Balanced RL
papers.tldr: OmniVL-Guard balances authenticity classification and manipulation localization to improve forgery analysis across interleaved text, images, and videos.

papers.title: PMSPO: Progressive Matching and Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization for Camouflaged Object Detection
papers.tldr: PMSPO combines multi-object matching, sample filtering, and semantic rewards to lead the evaluated reinforcement-learning methods on camouflaged-object benchmarks.

papers.title: Prism-MoE: Efficient Dense-to-MoE Conversion for Visual Autoregressive Generation
papers.tldr: Prism-MoE converts dense visual generators into sparse expert models with under 10% of the standard training budget and comparable generation quality.

papers.title: Probabilistic Salient Object Ranking
papers.tldr: ProbSOR predicts uncertain attention shifts between objects and introduces a dataset and metric for evaluating probabilistic visual-attention rankings.

papers.title: Prompt Tuning for CLIP on the Pretrained Manifold
papers.tldr: ManiPT constrains prompt tuning near CLIP's pretrained representation geometry to reduce overfitting and improve transfer.

papers.title: RefChess: Training-Free Contextual Search for Zero-Shot Referring Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: RefChess improves training-free referring image segmentation by searching how candidate masks behave across distractor contexts.

papers.title: Referring Multiple Regions with Large Multimodal Models via Contextual Latent Steering
papers.tldr: CSteer edits internal representations at inference to improve contextual understanding of multiple image regions without additional training.

papers.title: Respecting Modality Gap in Post-hoc Out-of-distribution Detection with Pre-trained Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper learns visual class prototypes from unlabeled test streams to mitigate a modality gap that prompt engineering alone cannot eliminate.

papers.title: Robust Cross-Modal Retrieval via Generative Semantic Refinement and Exclusion-Guided Adaptation
papers.tldr: ReEx improves noisy cross-modal retrieval by controlling language-model query repairs and learning from unlikely matches even when queries are ambiguous.

papers.title: RTPrune: Reading-Twice Inspired Token Pruning for Efficient DeepSeek-OCR Inference
papers.tldr: RTPrune follows DeepSeek-OCR’s two-stage reading pattern to reduce visual tokens while preserving accuracy and accelerating prefill.

papers.title: Saliency-Aware Model Merging
papers.tldr: SA-Merging combines task-specific models using connectivity-aware saliency and expert agreement, with support for low-rank adapters.

papers.title: SCoA: Revisiting Domain Generalized Object Detection with Style-Conditioned Adaptation
papers.tldr: SCoA conditions detector adaptation and object queries on visual style to improve generalization from one training domain to unseen domains.

papers.title: Seeing to Generalize: How Visual Data Corrects Binding Shortcuts
papers.tldr: Visual training can replace positional retrieval shortcuts with more robust symbolic binding, improving text-only generalization in controlled experiments.

papers.title: Self-Captioning Multimodal Interaction Tuning: Amplifying Exploitable Redundancies for Robust Vision Language Models
papers.tldr: A self-captioning workflow increases shared image–text information, with findings suggesting fewer visually induced errors and improved consistency.

papers.title: Semantic Impact–Driven Visual Scheduling for Vision Language Models
papers.tldr: SIVS schedules visual keys and values by their impact on predictions, reporting 87% compression while retaining over 99% of model performance.

papers.title: Skip-It? Theoretical Conditions for Layer Skipping in Vision–Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper develops interpretable redundancy conditions for layer skipping in vision-language models and validates their relationship to performance degradation.

papers.title: SpecPL: Disentangling Spectral Granularity for Prompt Learning
papers.tldr: SpecPL improves prompt learning by separating stable visual semantics from fine details and training with counterfactual detail changes.

papers.title: SpecPrune-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Models via Action-Aware Self-Speculative Pruning
papers.tldr: SpecPrune-VLA combines action history, layer importance, and motion-aware control to accelerate inference with negligible reported success-rate degradation.

papers.title: Spectral Heat Flow for Conservative Token Condensation in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: SpecFlow compresses visual tokens through graph-based importance, spatial coverage, and information aggregation, retaining strong performance under heavy pruning.

papers.title: SPLIT-VLM: Salience-Guided Partitioning towards Local Coverage for Importance-Aware Token Dropping in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: SPLIT reduces visual tokens by combining importance, local coverage, and diversity, retaining substantial accuracy even under severe token budgets.

papers.title: SS-TPT: Stability and Suitability-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Adversarially Robust Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: SS-TPT scores augmented image views for stability and suitability, improving adversarial robustness relative to inference throughput in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: StableVLA: Towards Robust Vision-Language-Action Models without Extra Data
papers.tldr: A small information-bottleneck adapter improves vision-language-action robustness to unseen visual disturbances without extra data or augmentation.

papers.title: Test-Time Debiasing with Probabilistic Prompts via Wasserstein Distance in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: W4D uses probabilistic prompts and Wasserstein distribution alignment to improve the fairness–utility trade-off of vision-language models at test time.

papers.title: TGV-KV: Text-Grounded KV Eviction for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: TGV-KV uses text-guided budgeting, ranking, and retention to shrink vision-language model caches while preserving accuracy in evaluated settings.

papers.title: The Geometry of Representational Failures in Vision Language Models
papers.tldr: Steerable visual concept vectors reveal a strong correlation between representational overlap and specific vision-language model errors.

papers.title: Towards Fine-Grained Robustness: Attention-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: A-TPT uses attention-guided image augmentation and prompt tuning to improve vision-language predictions on adversarial and clean inputs.

papers.title: Towards Multimodal Large Language Models with Both Training and Inference Efficiency
papers.tldr: SAISA removes redundant visual-token attention and aligns visual features directly to attention inputs, improving performance and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Transporting Task Vectors across Different Architectures without Training
papers.tldr: Theseus transfers task updates between different-width models by matching their effects on representations, without additional training.

papers.title: TranX-Adapter: Bridging Artifacts and Semantics within MLLMs for Robust AI-generated Image Detection
papers.tldr: TranX-Adapter improves AI-generated image detection by exchanging artifact and semantic information through transport-based fusion and cross-attention.

papers.title: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
papers.tldr: Trifuse combines attention, recognized text, and icon captions to improve GUI grounding without task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Multi-Modal Remote Sensing Detection Via Language-Pivoted Pretraining
papers.tldr: BabelRS aligns remote-sensing modalities through shared language concepts before detection training, improving stability and reported detection performance.

papers.title: Unveiling the Visual Counting Bottleneck in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Controlled counting experiments locate extrapolation failures in translating visual quantity into number tokens, despite preserved internal magnitude information.

papers.title: USE: A Unified Self-Ensembling Framework for Test-Time Prompt Tuning
papers.tldr: USE consistently combines original and augmented image predictions during prompt tuning and inference to improve test-time adaptation.

papers.title: VEQ: Modality-Adaptive Quantization for MoE Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: VEQ improves quantization of mixture-of-experts vision-language models by accounting for modality differences and unequal expert contributions.

papers.title: When Is Rank-1 Enough? Geometry-Guided Initialization for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.tldr: Gap-Init aligns rank-1 LoRA with a measured vision–text gap direction, stabilizing training and sometimes matching or exceeding rank-8 baselines.

papers.title: When RAG Hurts: Diagnosing and Mitigating Attention Distraction in Retrieval-Augmented LVLMs
papers.tldr: MAD-RAG preserves visual grounding during context integration, reducing cases where useful retrieved text distracts vision-language models from the image.

papers.title: Zooming without Zooming: Region-to-Image Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception
papers.tldr: Region-to-Image Distillation transfers supervision from zoomed-in teacher views to full-image students, improving fine-grained perception without inference-time tools.
